D1.name: User Mobility and Switching
D1.question: Can users leave the incumbent and adopt alternatives?
D1.mechanisms: Reduces default bias, switching costs, behavioral lock-in, manipulative choice architecture, and barriers to removing services or transferring user data.

D2.name: Rival Access and Distribution
D2.question: Can rivals enter, reach users, and distribute their services?
D2.mechanisms: Reduces restrictions on distribution, steering, commercial independence, contracting, and access to platform-controlled channels.

D3.name: Platform Neutrality and Non-Discrimination
D3.question: Can rivals compete fairly after obtaining access?
D3.mechanisms: Limits self-preferencing, discriminatory ranking or treatment, tying, bundling, and strategic use of non-public business-user information.

D4.name: Data, Interoperability, and Infrastructure Access
D4.question: Can rivals obtain the technical resources necessary to compete and scale?
D4.mechanisms: Reduces barriers arising from control over interfaces, infrastructure, interoperability, networks, and data; limits advantages from exclusive data accumulation and cross-service combination.

reportingRequirements.traceability: The underlying obligation-category and indicator scores must remain available so that users can trace aggregate results to the evidence and coding decisions from which they were constructed.
reportingRequirements.effectiveTogether: Effective Contestability must be reported alongside the De Jure and De Facto measures, never on its own.
